open_risks.text: The SPEC currently lives only in this session's scratchpad, which is session-scoped and is deleted when the session ends. If it is not copied into the repo as the first action, the entire specification is lost and this thread has no source of truth.

The .windful-ocean repo is PUBLIC and the logbook ledger is pushed to a _ledger branch on its origin. The confidential project codename that appears in the incident transcript paths must never be written into any tracked file, decision record, session entry or artifact pointer. Refer to the incident only by session uuid cfdbeee9.

Routing cannot be made deterministic. With the brief-length gate removed there is no categorical check that stops a cold dispatch which should have been a fork; SPEC section 10.1 accepts this because the default now fails toward main doing the work and the entry invariant makes a wrong dispatch halt loudly.

maxTurns is a threshold and is admitted as such. Its values are measured rather than chosen, but if a legitimate agent ever hits one the value is wrong and must be re-derived from observation, never overridden case by case.

Agent definition edits do not reach dispatches made in the same session: disk showed 14 sections while a dispatched agent reported 13. Any acceptance check that dispatches a just-edited agent tests the previous definition. Restart before verifying criteria 9, 10 and 11.

Fork is unavailable in the Claude desktop app Code tab (entrypoint claude-desktop) and available in terminal CLI sessions. The self-test is whether the Agent tool exposes run_in_background: if it does, fork mode is off. Implementation and verification should happen in a CLI session.

The acceptance checks in SPEC section 8 prove the configuration is applied, not that it is better. Proving improvement needs a comparable unit of work run afterwards, measured on agents per unit, wall-clock per unit, and peak main-thread context.

Output-format compliance beyond the first field is advisory. Nothing enforces that an agent fills its sections honestly; the only mitigation is that a work-forcing field cannot be filled without doing the work.

open_risks.scope: SPEC sections 5.3, 2.1 and 10.4 - fork as a routing vehicle
open_risks.text: Fork is gated by a server-side feature flag, not by entrypoint. The binary carries isForkSubagentEnabled and tengu_fork_subagent_enabled. Probed in the desktop app: a fork dispatch fails hard with "Agent type 'fork' not found". No env var, settings key or local statsig cache exposes or overrides it. It cannot be switched on in desktop or off in CLI, and can flip either way with no release and no config change. A routing rule naming fork is a prose claim about a flag nobody here can read or set.

open_risks.scope: cost of the cross-surface parity requirement
open_risks.text: Dropping fork (option A) works against the SPEC's own primary objective. Section 1.3 names main-thread context occupancy as what this remediation reduces, and fork is the only vehicle that reduces it without a re-typed brief. Under option A, step-dependent high-volume work floods main on both surfaces and the fallback is harness summarization - a fidelity loss rather than a failure. No portable substitute exists: Explore is cold and does not carry the conversation.

open_risks.scope: SPEC section 5.2 and check 8.5; plan step 8
open_risks.text: BLOCKER B1: SPEC check 8.5 is unachievable as section 5.2 is written. The six kept rules total 11,698 bytes and CLAUDE.md is 2,070, so the subtotal is 13,768 against a 13,000 ceiling - 768 over before the new delegation rule (~900 B) or the section 5.4 prohibition are added. Real overshoot at step 8 is ~1,700 B. Section 1.2's stated target of ~2,520 tokens (~10,080 B) is missed by even more. Blocks step 8 only; steps 1-7 and 9 are unaffected. Three resolutions costed in the plan; R2 recommended.

Compressing security.md and rescoping no-direct-db-access.md narrows what is always-on, with two gaps open by choice. vibesec triggers on web application code, so a non-web project gets no depth from it; mitigated by preloading vibesec into security-reviewer, which is dispatched regardless of project type. And block-destructive-bash.sh matches the Supabase CLI path only, not psql or a raw DATABASE_URL, so the general prohibition stays prose rather than deferring to the hook.

out_of_scope.text: Do not add a router agent or routing skill. SPEC section 11 rejects it: a new advisory layer for a decision that section 10.1 admits cannot be made deterministic.
Do not keep delivery-lead in reduced form. A depth limit of 1 makes the layer structurally impossible and a reduced Lead reintroduces a sequential pipeline stage.
Do not express token or cost budgets as prose rules. Budgets are enforced by roster size and the preamble cut, both structural.
Do not re-derive the incident measurements. They are recorded in the SPEC and re-measuring is a second error source, not confirmation.
Do not change any repository other than ~/.claude and its .windful-ocean checkout. The project the incident occurred on is out of scope entirely.
Do not adopt any routing rule whose behaviour differs between the CLI and the desktop app. The user requires identical configuration behaviour on both surfaces.
